title: Fourteen Springs and One Short String
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与社会·日常生活）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与社会·日常生活）　|　核心词汇：dozen　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dozen 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1937 my grandmother ① bought a dozen that no shopkeeper in the market would have counted, and she said the buying was the whole of the spring. The ② dozen, meaning the number and not the many, ran fourteen springs and stayed unnamed in the book; a dozen, she said, is the only thing in a market that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ dozen in that market had the same short string at the end of it, and the ④ dozen at the end, meaning the one they kept for the neighbour and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A dozen, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; my grandmother said the counting is the part that fills fourteen springs.

My aunt meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the dozen was the whole of the story, meaning the many and not the number. The ⑥ dozen, meaning the many and not any of that, is the only thing in a story that everybody counts and nobody finishes; dozen, she said, is either something you buy or the only word that means both a number and a many. She said the many is the part they remember.

By 1946 the ⑦ dozen had become a line in a bill, and the bill had become an argument about the short string. The ⑧ dozen of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in April, was one market and fourteen springs of counting; dozen, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to count. She said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ dozen I remember is the one named in the bill, which was sold in 1958 and is still described as the quietest in the market. A ⑩ dozen, my mother said in 1960, is the only one that improves by being counted; every dozen, she said, is a many that has agreed to look like a number. She said the many was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 一打；十二个（指那个市场里摆着的那一打）
B. n. 一打；十二个（指那个数目本身，与许多相对）
C. 固定搭配：buy a dozen 买一打
D. n. 一打；十二个（指留给邻居的那一打）
E. n. 一打；十来个（抽象总称，指一家人的采买之事）
F. n. 一打；十二个（指账单上写到、被列名的那一打）
G. n. 十来个；许多（指故事里人人都数却无人点清的那样东西）
H. n. 许多（抽象总称，指人人都数却无人点清的那种数量）

items.q: bought a dozen that no shopkeeper in the market would have counted
The dozen, meaning the number and not the many
the dozen was the whole of the story
the dozen had become a line in a bill
The dozen of the whole thing
A dozen, my mother said in 1960

answers.why: buy a dozen 意为“买一打”，1937 年祖母买了一打，那个市场里没有一位店主肯把它数清。
dozen 意为“一打、十二个”，指那个数目本身而不是许多，它经过了十四个春天而在簿子上没有被记名。
dozen 意为“一打、十二个”，指那个市场里的每一打，每一打到头来都有同一根短短的绳子。
dozen 意为“一打、十二个”，指留给邻居的那一打，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
dozen 意为“十来个、许多”，指故事里人人都数却无人点清的那样东西，姑姑说这许多就是那个故事的全部。
dozen 意为“许多”，指人人都数却无人点清的那种数量而不是那个数目，是故事里人人都数、却无人点清的东西。
dozen 意为“一打、十二个”，指账单上写到、被列名的那一打，到 1946 年这一打成了账单里的一行。
dozen 意为“一打、十来个”，祖母四月写道，整件事的采买之事是一个市场和十四个春天的点数。
dozen 意为“一打、十二个”，我记得的是账单上列名的那一打，1958 年卖掉了，至今仍被说成市场里最安静的一打。
dozen 为抽象总称，母亲 1960 年说，一打是唯一会因为被好好点数而变得更好的东西。
